title: Export text-to-binary resource conversion resets saved `Packed*Array` values to their array-literal script defaults
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf]
- Not tested in other versions (only 4.7.2.stable is installed here; the behaviour is in the export-time `.tres` → `.res` conversion path, which exists in every 4.x release).

### System information

macOS 15.7.2 (Apple Silicon, arm64) - Godot v4.7.2.stable - headless export + headless `--main-pack` run (no renderer involved; Linux/X11 preset used for the PCK, same result with macOS and Web presets)

### Issue description

When a project is exported with the default `editor/export/convert_text_resources_to_binary=true`, every `@export` property declared as a `Packed*Array` **with an array-literal default** (`= []` or `= [1.0, 2.0]`) loses the value saved in the `.tres` file: loading the exported resource from the PCK returns the script default instead.

Properties declared without an initializer (`@export var b: PackedInt32Array`), with an explicit constructor (`= PackedFloat32Array()`), or as a typed Array (`@export var d: Array[int] = []`) keep their saved values. Saving the same resource with `ResourceSaver.save(res, "res://saved.res")` in editor mode and reloading it also keeps every value, so the binary resource format itself is fine; only the export-time text → binary conversion is affected. Exporting with the flag set to `false` preserves everything.

Test resource (`packed_fixture.gd` + `fixture.tres` in the MRP):

```gdscript
extends Resource
class_name PackedFixture

@export var a: PackedInt32Array = []
@export var b: PackedInt32Array
@export var c: PackedFloat32Array = PackedFloat32Array()
@export var d: Array[int] = []
@export var e: PackedFloat32Array = []
@export var f: PackedFloat32Array = [1.0, 2.0]
```

| Field | Declaration | Saved in `.tres` / editor / direct `.res` | Loaded from PCK, conversion **on** | Loaded from PCK, conversion off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | `PackedInt32Array = []` | `[3, 5, 7]` | **`[]`** | `[3, 5, 7]` |
| b | `PackedInt32Array` (no initializer) | `[11, 13]` | `[11, 13]` | `[11, 13]` |
| c | `PackedFloat32Array = PackedFloat32Array()` | `[0.25, 0.75]` | `[0.25, 0.75]` | `[0.25, 0.75]` |
| d | `Array[int] = []` | `[17, 19]` | `[17, 19]` | `[17, 19]` |
| e | `PackedFloat32Array = []` | `[0.125, 0.875]` | **`[]`** | `[0.125, 0.875]` |
| f | `PackedFloat32Array = [1.0, 2.0]` | `[9.0, 8.0]` | **`[1.0, 2.0]`** | `[9.0, 8.0]` |

The failing cases are exactly the ones whose default is an array literal, which GDScript types as a plain `Array` before converting it to the declared `Packed*Array`; the ones with a real `Packed*Array` default (or none) survive. Every export and load finished with exit code 0 and no script or engine error, so nothing warns about the lost data.

In a real project this silently reverted 13 data fields (spawn weights, region layout, timers) to their script defaults in every exported build while the editor run was correct: a 600-frame headless boot of the exported PCK passed, only the gameplay data was wrong.

**Expected:** the exported resource preserves all six saved property values, as it does when the conversion is disabled.

**Workaround:** set `editor/export/convert_text_resources_to_binary=false` in `project.godot`, or give such properties an explicit `Packed*Array()` default instead of an array literal.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Unzip the attached MRP. Its `project.godot` sets `editor/export/convert_text_resources_to_binary=true` (the default) and `export_presets.cfg` contains a `Linux/X11` preset. Export templates for 4.7.2 must be installed.
2. `godot --headless --path . --import`
3. `godot --headless --path . --export-pack 'Linux/X11' out.pck`
4. `godot --headless --main-pack out.pck -s "$PWD/repro_read.gd"` (the reader script is passed by absolute OS path, so it does not need to be inside the PCK). It loads `res://fixture.tres` and prints every field.
   - Actual: `REPRO: source=res://fixture.tres a=[] b=[11, 13] c=[0.25, 0.75] d=[17, 19] e=[] f=[1.0, 2.0]`
   - Expected: `a=[3, 5, 7] b=[11, 13] c=[0.25, 0.75] d=[17, 19] e=[0.125, 0.875] f=[9.0, 8.0]`
5. Set the flag to `false` in `project.godot`, repeat steps 3–4: every value now matches the `.tres`.
6. (Control, no export) `godot --headless --path . -s "$PWD/repro_read.gd" -- --save-res` saves the resource as `res://saved.res` with `ResourceSaver` and reloads it: all six values are preserved, so the binary format alone is not the problem.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

MRP attached below (`packed_array_export_mrp.zip`, 4 KB): `project.godot` (conversion flag set to `true`), `packed_fixture.gd`, `fixture.tres`, `repro_read.gd`, a `Linux/X11` export preset and a `README.md` with the three commands. Nothing else is required; no scenes are opened and no renderer is used.

[packed_array_export_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33398496/packed_array_export_mrp.zip)
